title: Two-object localization pullback has contractible mapping spaces
statement: Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], geometric realization and weak contractibility [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and weak homotopy equivalences, Kan fibrations and model-structure terminology [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]. A simplicial category has mapping simplicial sets, associative simplicial composition and identity vertices; its category $\pi_0$ has the same objects and path components of realized mapping sets as arrows. A vertex is a homotopy equivalence if its component is invertible in this category. Write $\mathrm{sCat}_{\{x,y\}}$ for these categories on two distinct labelled objects and functors equal to the identity on the labels, with the mappingwise model structure obtained by the four-sort theory of composition and units. Let $E'$ be such a simplicial category, and let $e\in E'(x,y)_0$ be a homotopy equivalence. Define $E(a,b)\subseteq E'(a,b)$ to consist of the simplices all of whose vertices are homotopy equivalences. Composition and identities restrict to these subsets, defining a simplicial subcategory $E$ with $e\in E(x,y)_0$. Let $F$ be the discrete walking-arrow simplicial category on $x,y$, and let $F\to E$ send its arrow to $e$. Choose functorial cofibrant replacements $\widetilde F\to F$, $\widetilde E\to E$ in $\mathrm{sCat}_{\{x,y\}}$, with $\widetilde F\to F$ an isomorphism, and use naturality to get $F\cong\widetilde F\to\widetilde E$. For a simplicial category $C$, its degreewise groupoid completion $C^{-1}C$ is obtained by formally adjoining inverses to all arrows in each degree, with simplicial operators induced by their universal properties. Factor the induced functor $\widetilde F^{-1}\widetilde F\to\widetilde E^{-1}\widetilde E$ as a mappingwise weak-equivalence cofibration $\widetilde F^{-1}\widetilde F\to Z$ followed by a mappingwise Kan fibration $Z\to\widetilde E^{-1}\widetilde E$. Form $G=\widetilde E\times_{\widetilde E^{-1}\widetilde E}Z$, whose mapping sets are the corresponding simplicial pullbacks. Then the compatible maps from $F$ into $\widetilde E$ and $Z$ induce a labelled factorization $F\to G\to E\hookrightarrow E'$ of the prescribed map $F\to E'$, and all four mapping simplicial sets of $G$ are weakly contractible.

source.place: Bergner, Lemma 4.1 and the construction preceding Lemma 4.2, printed pp. 13–14

proof.text: First check the homotopy-equivalence subcategory rather than assuming it is a simplicial groupoid. The vertices of any simplex of $E'(a,b)$ lie in one path component, since they are joined by its realized edges. Hence the selected simplices are stable under faces and degeneracies. Their composites are selected because compositions of invertible morphisms in $\pi_0E'$ are invertible; identities are selected as well. Moreover $|E(a,b)|$ is exactly the union of the invertible path components of $|E'(a,b)|$, with their original topology. Indeed the realization quotient in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] has a continuous map to the discrete set $\pi_0|E'(a,b)|$, constant on each simplex; the selected union is open and closed, and restricting a quotient map to the inverse image of an open subset is again a quotient map. Thus paths witnessing equality between selected components stay inside $|E(a,b)|$. Every component has a vertex representative, since a point represented in a simplex is joined within that simplex to a vertex. Every inverse component of a selected vertex is itself selected, and the two inverse equations, witnessed in $E'$, consequently hold in $\pi_0E$. Therefore every arrow of $\pi_0E$ is invertible, and $e$ supplies the specified functor $F\to E$.

source.place: Section 4 opening, printed p.13: restriction to homotopy equivalences; elementary expansion from the realization quotient.

proof.text: Put $q:\widetilde E\to E$. By the meaning of cofibrant replacement in the mappingwise model structure [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model], $\widetilde E$ is cofibrant and $q$ induces bijections on all component sets. For a component $[u]:a\to b$ of $\widetilde E$, choose the component $[v]:b\to a$ corresponding under $q$ to $[q(u)]^{-1}$. Injectivity on components gives $[v][u]=1_a$ and $[u][v]=1_b$. Thus $\pi_0\widetilde E$ is a groupoid. Naturality of the chosen replacements, using the assumed isomorphism $\widetilde F\cong F$, gives a functor $u:F\to\widetilde E$ with $qu$ equal to the prescribed $F\to E$.

source.place: Section 4 opening, printed p.13: functorial cofibrant replacement and its naturality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cofibrant-homotopy-groupoid-completion] to $A=\widetilde E$ and $O=\{x,y\}$. Cofibrancy is part of the chosen replacement, and the groupoid hypothesis was proved in step 2. It follows that the canonical map $j:\widetilde E\to\widetilde E^{-1}\widetilde E$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping simplicial set. This is a mappingwise assertion, stronger than a weak equivalence of realized nerves.

source.place: Lemma 4.1, printed p.14: use of Dwyer–Kan [4, Proposition 9.5].

proof.text: Let $B=\widetilde E^{-1}\widetilde E$ and $J=\widetilde F^{-1}\widetilde F\cong F^{-1}F$. In each degree $F^{-1}F$ has precisely $1_x,1_y,g,g^{-1}$: any composable word in $g,g^{-1}$ reduces by adjacent cancellations to the unique arrow with its prescribed endpoints. All its simplicial operators are identities, so $J(a,b)=\Delta^0$ for every pair $a,b$. In the stipulated factorization $J\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}B$, $i$ is a mappingwise weak equivalence and $p$ a mappingwise Kan fibration. Consequently every $Z(a,b)$ has one path component and zero positive homotopy groups, because $i(a,b)$ induces bijections/isomorphisms on these invariants. Equivalently every $Z(a,b)$ is weakly contractible in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Keep $Z$ as the replacement; the original map $J\to B$ need not be a fibration.

source.place: Section 4, printed p.13, factorization through Z; Lemma 4.1, printed p.14, calculation of the four mapping sets of F inverse F.

proof.text: For each labelled pair $a,b$, the projection $G(a,b)\to Z(a,b)$ is the pullback of $j(a,b):\widetilde E(a,b)\to B(a,b)$ along the Kan fibration $p(a,b):Z(a,b)\to B(a,b)$. By the right-properness clause of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and step 3 this projection is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 4 then gives one component and trivial positive homotopy groups for $G(a,b)$ as well, so its map to $\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This proves weak contractibility of all four mapping sets, without assuming that $B$, $Z$ or $\widetilde E$ is locally Kan.

source.place: Lemma 4.1, printed p.14: right properness, applied directly to the four simplicial pullback squares.

proof.text: The two functors from $F$ are $u:F\to\widetilde E$ and $F\to J\xrightarrow{i}Z$. Their composites to $B$ agree: both are $F\xrightarrow{u}\widetilde E\xrightarrow{j}B$, by functoriality of degreewise completion and $pi:J\to B$ being the functor being factored. The pullback therefore gives $F\to G$ explicitly, sending each arrow to the pair of its two images. Pairwise composition, identities and simplicial operators agree because they do in each coordinate. Composing with $G\to\widetilde E\xrightarrow{q}E\hookrightarrow E'$ recovers $F\to E'$ since $qu$ is the prescribed functor. All maps fix the labels, which proves the stated factorization.

source.place: Section 4, printed pp.13–14: pullback square and the factorization of the prescribed walking-arrow map.

(5) the orientation is right: G(a,b)→Z(a,b) is the pullback of the weak equivalence j along the Kan fibration p, so right properness of lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper applies. (6) the pullback factorization is coordinatewise and recovers qu. The new node is true and is the sufficient direction of DK 9.5.
